description.en: R. Yohanan Hasandlar was born in Egypt, but moved to the Land of Israel where he became a devoted student of R. Akiva. Even when the latter was in a Roman jail, R. Yochanan found a way to come to him for instruction.
description.he: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר נולד במצרים, עלה לארץ ישראל והיה לתלמידו של רבי עקיבא. גם כאשר רבי עקיבא היה כלוא בידי הרומאים, מצא רבי יוחנן דרך להגיע אליו כדי ללמוד אצלו.

en.title: The Devotion of Rabbi Yohanan Hasandlar
en.prompt: The deep respect and camaraderie among the sages, particularly highlighting the unique devotion and service of Rabbi Yohanan the Alexandrian to Rabbi Akiva, as well as the collaborative and respectful nature of their scholarly discussions and actions. The Jerusalem Talmud, a central text of Rabbinic Judaism and a compilation of teachings and discussions of Jewish law, records a discussion among prominent sages about religious laws and practices, reflecting the scholarly debates and interpretations that are foundational to Jewish legal tradition.

en.title: A Disguised Visit to Resolve Halachah
en.prompt: Rabbi Yohanan Hasandlar's cleverness and dedication to Jewish law are exemplified in his disguised visit to Rabbi Akiva in prison to resolve a halachic question. The Jerusalem Talmud, an ancient corpus of law, ethics, and stories from the land of Israel, recounts this incident, highlighting the importance of the ḥalîṣah ceremony and the lengths to which sages would go to uphold Jewish law.

en.title: Staying in the Land of Israel
en.prompt: Rabbi Yochanan the Sandal-Maker chose to remain in the Land of Israel despite the dire political and economic conditions following the Bar Kokhba revolt. This narrative explores the internal conflict and ultimate decision of Rabbi Yochanan, a second-century sage and student of Rabbi Akiva, to stay in his homeland.
